newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian farmers threaten suicide over Yanni show.
newsitem.headline: Indian farmers threaten suicide over Yanni show.

text.p: Five Indian farmers have threatened to set themselves on fire as protests mount against a series of concerts this week by Greek-born musician Yanni in front of the Taj Mahal monument.

The farmers, who say their crops were destroyed to build a stage for the concert, say they will immolate themselves at the site on Thursday, the day of Yanni's first performance, unless the government pays adequate compensation.
Their threats follow protests from conservationists who say the government is turning a blind eye to the potential damage that the New Age composer's concerts can cause to the 17th-century monument.

Environmental activist Mahesh Chandra Mehta has filed a petition asking the Supreme Court to shift the venue of performances, to be held on March 20, 21 and 22. The court is due to hear the plea before Thursday.
India's Central Pollution Control Board says the concert on the banks of the river violates a court order banning activity within a 500-metre (540-yard) "green belt" around the Taj Mahal.

In a separate petition, a prominent historian, journalists and social activists last week asked the court to stop the concerts, saying that the sound, light and fuel emissions generated by the performances could damage the mausoleum.

Environmental activists, led by Mehta, have campaigned hard in recent years to save the Taj Mahal from "marble cancer". They say the Taj Mahal, built by a lovelorn emperor in memory of his wife who died in childbirth, is yellowing due to pollution.
Ironically, Yanni has pledged to donate the proceeds from the concert, estimated at up to $3 million, to the Uttar Pradesh state government for the Taj Mahal's maintenance and preservation.
Organisers of the concerts say they are taking pains to ensure that the performances will not damage the monument.

Yanni Management Inc officials say they plan to use a lighting system that will ensure that no light rays fall on the monument behind the orchestra, and use audio equipment that transmits sound away from the Taj.
Yanni's concerts are to be held on a specially built stage in front of the Taj Mahal.
The Indian army is erecting two temporary bridges to enable concertgoers to cross the Yamuna river and face the stage.
Villagers who farm in the river bed have been forced to uproot about 100 hectares (250 acres) of crops to make way for the stage and extensive security for Yanni and an estimated 22,000 concertgoers.

Last November a group of feminists threatened to set themselves alight in protest against the Miss World beauty pageant, which they said was demeaning to women and Indian culture. But they did not carry out their threats.
